title: agents-cooperation config
description: Owner agent scheduling config. Structure lives here; cross-object rules (references, kind-specific effort sets, launch support per kind, one enabled owner per engine, parallel limits) are enforced by scripts/agents-config.ts validate.

engines.description: Agent CLI engines keyed by engine id.

owners.description: Owner agents keyed by owner id. Each enabled engine has at most one enabled owner.

workers.description: Workers keyed by worker id; every id ends with _worker.

herdr.description: Herdr dispatch settings for heterogeneous (herdr) workers and collaborating owners.

worker_session.description: Name of the TUI-less Herdr session that hosts every herdr worker lane; owners and collaborating owners stay in the user's main session.

max_wait_minutes.description: Longest single wait for a herdr agent, in minutes; resolve exposes it as wait_timeout_ms and every herdr wait must pass it as --timeout.

effort.description: Engine-native effort. Allowed set depends on the engine kind: claude low|medium|high|xhigh|max; codex minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max; grok none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max; other kinds (e.g. opencode, whose --variant is provider/model specific) any non-empty string. Checked by the script.

native_subagents.description: Whether the engine can spawn sub-agents natively. Only claude and codex can.

workers.description: Worker ids in priority order; resolve --class judgment takes the first available non-free one (with --tag: the first available heterogeneous one carrying the domain tag, else the owner's native worker); free class workers are taken by resolve --class mechanical|routine.

max_parallel.description: Cap on workers (native and herdr) running concurrently for this owner; the owner enforces it by counting running ledger entries.

tags.description: mechanical and routine are reserved class tags: a worker carrying one is a free worker that resolve --class mechanical|routine picks first (at most one of the two; any engine, native when it matches the owner's). Every other tag is a domain tag describing the model's strengths; resolve --class judgment --tag <t> uses it only to pick a heterogeneous worker (a different engine than the owner), falling back to the owner's native worker.
